claim: tools/bus/bus.py passes its own unit selftest, and that selftest is proven able to fail: every plausible regression in its mutation spec, applied one at a time to a copy of the module, is caught
source: 2026-07-25: the selftest found two real defects on first run. cmd_inbox filtered from_lane == lane, which made 8 of the bus's 9 messages permanently undeliverable because lane B had addressed durable notes to lane B. And a torn append ate the FOLLOWING message, because the next write concatenated onto a fragment with no trailing newline. | 2026-07-25 correction: this claim used to read "passes its own 12-check selftest". The count was never checked by the verifier (bus.py selftest exits 0 on all-pass and reports no count) and went false within a day when the selftest reached 35 checks. A claim whose text asserts more than its command checks is the unverifiable wish this ledger exists to reject. The count is now out of the text; what replaced it is a property the mutation harness actually holds. The verifier moved from bus.py selftest to tools/bus/mutation_check.py in the same pass, because the rewritten text asserts the mutation property and selftest never checked it; leaving it would have reproduced the defect being fixed. C-019 still binds the selftest. 2026-07-25, second pass: the harness moved from tools/bus/mutation_check.py to tools/audit/mutate.py --spec bus. It was bus-specific and the same hole existed in tools/refute/refute.py, so one driver now reads specs from tools/audit/mutations/. The mutant is written BESIDE the target rather than in %TEMP%, because refute.py runs verifiers with cwd=ROOT and a temp copy gets a ROOT that does not exist: every case then turns BROKEN and every mutation looks caught for a reason unrelated to the check under test, which is a harness manufacturing its own green. A count was removed from this claim text on 2026-07-25: the verifier requires every mutation in the spec to be applied and caught and now fails an empty spec, but it does not assert how many mutations exist, so a number here would again assert more than the command checks and would go stale the moment the spec grows. That is exactly how the original '12-check selftest' wording went false.

claim: an edit to a past bus row is detectable, is marked on BOTH read paths rather than delivered as authentic, and a merge that drops an earlier line no longer loses an unread message
source: 2026-07-25, found by reading bus.py against block/buzz's signed-event model. Two defects were reproduced as a failing oracle before anything changed. (1) A third party edited a delivered row's body from 'gate is RED, do not ship' to 'gate is GREEN, ship it' and the bus handed lane C the edited text with nothing marking it as altered: a row that does not commit to its content cannot be told apart from one never touched. (2) The read cursor was a positional offset, which assumes no earlier row ever moves; state/bus.jsonl is git-tracked with two writers (tools/bus/bus.py, tools/dolt/client.py), so a hand-resolved merge dropping one line shifted every lane's cursor and delivered NOTHING where an unread message existed. Scope stated in the module docstring and in verify's own output: tamper EVIDENT not tamper proof, authenticates nobody because every lane is the same OS user, and truncation of the newest rows is undetectable from the log alone. 35 checks, up from 12.

It does NOT fail on the 12 rows that predate chaining, because failing on pre-existing traffic would make the clean state unreachable; --strict is the opt-in for a caller that wants the whole log chained, and it exits 1 today. claim: refute.py distinguishes an empty ledger from a filter that matched nothing, and a verifier that could not run does not read as a pass
source: 2026-07-25. Two exit-0-while-checking-nothing defects in the refutation engine itself, found while registering unrelated bus claims. (1) `refute.py run --only C-019,C-020` printed 'no claims to check. seed state/claims-verify.jsonl first.' and exited 0 against a ledger holding 20 claims, because --only is a substring match and the comma list matched none of them: a caller asking for specific claims and silently getting none was told its claims held. It now exits 2 and names the count and the match rule; an empty ledger stays 0 because a fresh install is not a failure. (2) BROKEN was printed as 'not a pass' and then excluded from the exit code, so a verifier that timed out, named an unknown shell, or carried no command at all read as success to anything binding on the exit code, making breakage the cheapest way to silence this tool. Exit is now REFUTED plus BROKEN, with --allow-broken as a named hatch someone has to type. 15 checks, including the negative cases (the filter must still filter; expect=fail must still invert) and an assertion that the real ledger and results file were not written by the selftest, since a selftest that appended to state/refutations.jsonl would manufacture the evidence the rest of the system trusts.

claim: the undo path for writes into ~/.claude refuses to capture a denied or secret-bearing file, and its own checks are proven able to fail
source: 2026-07-25. This exists because sync-live-settings.py's backup was a fixed-name one-deep copy: the second run destroyed the only pristine copy, and the other live-only files under ~/.claude had no backup at all. Scope of what this command proves, stated so the claim does not assert more than it checks: snap.py's selftest plants its OWN live tree in a temp directory and never reads the real ~/.claude, so a pass here is evidence about the tool's rules, not about the contents of any real snapshot. The mutation spec breaks, one at a time, the collision loop whose absence WAS the original defect, each of the three deny rules, both directions of the secret filter, every verify failure mode including the policy half (an entry the current deny lists would now refuse, snapshot content its manifest never mentions, and captured bytes that match a secret pattern on re-scan), every drift class, and each of restore's refusals. Two fixture notes that are load-bearing: a deny check no candidate path can reach is decorative, which is why the denied name and denied suffix cases sit NESTED inside allowlisted trees with clean content, and the take-refuses-to-overwrite guard sits behind the collision loop, so the selftest stubs the id generator to put the guard rather than the mechanism under test. No count appears above for the same reason as C-022.

claim: the snapshot taken before the pending live settings.json write is still intact and still policy-compliant, so that write remains revertable
source: 2026-07-25. C-024 proves the tool's rules; this row is about one real snapshot of the real tree, which is the thing that actually makes the classifier-blocked live write revertable. It fails if a captured file changed or vanished, if content ever appears for a hash-only entry, if the snapshot holds a file its own manifest never mentions, if any entry would be denied under the CURRENT deny lists (deny lists grow, and an old snapshot does not retroactively become compliant), or if any captured file's bytes match a secret pattern on re-scan. That last check is the one worth having: the take already applied the filter, so re-asking catches a take whose filter was wrong or a pattern added since. Only the pattern NAME is ever printed. Local-only by construction: state/snapshots/.gitignore excludes */files/, so the manifest is committed and the captured content is not.

claim: the plain-language rules this repo writes status updates and blocker lists under are enforced by a checker whose every rule is proven able to fire, and proven able to stay quiet on text sitting exactly on its limit
source: 2026-07-25. A style rule nothing measures is a wish, and this repo has shipped several: the rule and its violation looked identical from outside. So explain-simply ships an executable checker and this row is what keeps the checker honest. Scope of what this command proves, stated so the claim does not assert more than it checks: it measures the SHAPE of writing (sentence length, active-voice share, hidden verbs, acronyms before expansion, jargon, and this repo's own rule that a numeral in prose must appear in code somewhere in the same document, which exists because the retracted 24-to-64 figure sat in resume copy for weeks with nothing behind it). It cannot tell whether a passing document is TRUE, and a draft can pass every check here and still bury the failure or hand the operator a blocker with no command attached. Two fixture classes are load-bearing. Boundary flips are what human review misses, so every threshold has a case planted exactly on it that must stay quiet: a sentence of exactly the word ceiling, an average exactly at the ceiling, exactly half the sentences active (the rule needs MORE than half), and a paragraph at exactly the sentence ceiling. Reachability kills are the failure this repo has actually shipped, so each table and each regex is made unmatchable in turn. The passive check is ADVISORY by design: passive detection is a heuristic that over-reports, and an over-reporting detector with a zero threshold gets ignored or deleted, so only the ratio can fail a run and one mutation promotes the advisory to a violation to prove that stays true. The checker found a real defect in itself when first run on its own SKILL.md: a run of bullets was measured as one long paragraph. Both the selftest and the skill's own document are wired into the falsifiability job in .github/workflows/ship-gate.yml. No count appears above for the same reason as C-024.
